data.title: Bosch opens special window to regularise legacy physical share transfers
data.description:
Bosch Limited ( (IN:BOSCHLTD) ) has shared an update.

Bosch Limited has notified stock exchanges that it has published a newspaper notice announcing a special window for re-lodgement of transfer deeds for physical shares. The window applies to transfer requests originally lodged before April 1, 2019, that were rejected, returned or left unattended due to deficiencies in documentation or process, offering affected shareholders another opportunity to regularise such transfers in line with SEBI’s latest circular.

The move underscores Bosch’s effort to align with evolving SEBI regulations governing physical share transfers and to clean up legacy issues in its share registry. By formally communicating the window through exchanges and a national business daily, the company seeks to improve transparency, protect investor interests and facilitate smoother transition toward a fully compliant, largely dematerialised shareholding structure.

data.title: Saray Matbaacilik Scales Back Rights Issue, Halves Planned Capital Increase
data.description:
Saray Matbaacilik Kagitcilik Kirtasiyecilik Ticaret Ve Sanayi A.S. ( (TR:SAMAT) ) has shared an announcement.

Saray Matbaacilik Kagitcilik Kirtasiyecilik Ticaret Ve Sanayi A.S. has updated its rights issue plan, now targeting a 100% cash capital increase that will lift paid-in capital from TRY 112.4 million to TRY 224.8 million, rather than the previously proposed 200% hike to TRY 337.2 million. All 112.4 million new shares, split between A group registered and B group bearer stock, will be issued as dematerialized securities at a nominal price of TRY 1 per share and allocated in line with existing share classes.

Shareholders’ preemptive rights are fully preserved, with a 15-day subscription period to acquire new shares at par, and any remaining stock to be sold on Borsa Istanbul’s primary market for two business days before unsold shares are cancelled under the relevant share communiqué. By filing a revised prospectus and related documents with the Capital Markets Board, the company is recalibrating its equity-raising scale, which may reduce potential dilution compared with the earlier plan while still bolstering its capital base and underscoring adherence to Turkish capital markets and corporate law requirements.

data.title: Entero Healthcare Subsidiary Pays GST Penalty Under Protest, Plans Refund Claim
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Entero Healthcare Solutions Limited ( (IN:ENTERO) ).

Entero Healthcare Solutions has disclosed that its subsidiary, ACE Cardiopathy Solutions, has been hit with a Goods and Services Tax penalty by the Uttar Pradesh GST Authority for non-generation of an e-invoice. The authority levied a monetary penalty of Rs. 12,91,728, which the subsidiary has paid under protest to secure immediate release of a vehicle and prevent further demurrage charges and operational losses.

The company emphasized that the penalty amount is not material to its consolidated financial position or overall operations, limiting the financial impact for shareholders. ACE Cardiopathy plans to seek recovery or refund of the penalty through available remedies under GST law, indicating that the issue is being treated as a compliance dispute rather than a structural business risk for Entero’s wider healthcare operations.

data.description:
